full_page.content:
c. 1930, April
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.
SAINT BONAVENTURE'S MONASTERY
DETROIT, MICHIGAN
Mrs. Margaret T. LeDoux 985 St. Mary Ave. San Leandro, California
My Dear Sister Margaret Therese ;-
God bless you and all yours! I do hope you are keeping well. Best wishes from all in Detroit - Francis Molloy & family, who were here yesterday; Doonans, Sampsons, etc,; also from our niece Mary Casey, Jim's daughter and of course from Father Maurice - now Fr. Joachim, O. F.M. Cap., of Huntington, Indiana. His address St.Felix Monastery Route 8. Thanks be to God he seems well and hopeful of making profession in September.
No doubt it must seem to you at times that I forget all about my one-time little sisters and brothers. I know I seldom write and am tardy in answering them when they write to me; at least I feel somewhat guilty that way. Be that as it may, I hardly think there is a day passes but what I remember you all. I have here before me letters started to the above S.M.T. Jan. 24th, Feb. 24 and March 25. That of Feb. nearly finished; yet ...? This ought to be a sort of indication that I at least sometimes do remember you. The fact of it is, I believe, that as time and distance separate me from the scenes and associations of my childhood and youth my recollections of both become sweeter and more reinviting -...! ... But ...! The future holds a better part, .... =
Surely we were fortunate children that the Good God gave us such sturdy, honest, virtuous parents. How can we ever be grateful enough? Thanks be to God! May their dear souls rest in the peace of the blessed! I often think of the wonderful designs of Divine Providence as revealed in the plans and strivings of these and simi- lar "children of St. Patrick" - so often pioneers indeed. In the case of our own dear Parents, e.g .; how they were directed from city-life in Boston and Philadelphia away to "The River Bank". At that time Prescot must have been little more than a village; and judging what the Eagle Rock - four, miles down the river - mist have been at that time from what it was 15 years later, when I stayed two weeks at Aunt Mary Ann's, cone might get an idea of what a perfect hermitage in the wilderness might be.
